moduleTitle: Automation shapes in the Case Life Cycle
learningObjectives: Explain how Automations perform system actions without user interaction, and how to add them
Identify the Automation shapes available in App Studio and choose the correct one for a requirement

elements.description: An action the system performs automatically — no user input required. Examples: send a confirmation email, create a child Case, copy data. Automations and Collect information steps are the two shape categories in a Case Life Cycle.

elements.text: Automation shapes are like robotic arms on an assembly line: instead of a human pressing a button to send a notification or run a calculation, the automation shape executes automatically when the process flow reaches that step — invisible to the end user but essential to the workflow. Remove one and the product comes out missing a component.

elements.description: Two paths to add an Automation shape:
items: Case Life Cycle view: select a Step → More → Automations
Process modeler: Add → Automations (then configure with parameters specific to its purpose)

elements.description: Two Step categories in a Pega workflow:
items: USER STEP (e.g., Collect information) — requires a person to act; creates an Assignment
AUTOMATION SHAPE — runs automatically when the Case reaches the Step; no user interaction needed

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Automation shapes available in App Studio

elements.description: Change to a Stage = move to a SPECIFIC Stage. Change to next Stage = advance automatically. Change to previous Stage = return to the previously visited Stage. Three distinct shapes — each behaves differently.

CREATE CASE — creates child Cases. UPDATE A CASE — updates current Case or all descendants. PERSIST CASE — converts a temporary Case to a permanent DB record. SEARCH DUPLICATE CASES — auto-checks for duplicate submissions.

ATTACH CONTENT — attaches file, URL, or note. CREATE PDF — creates a PDF from a specified View and attaches it. GENERATE DOCUMENT — generates Case documents. Note: Create PDF and Generate document are separate shapes.

SEND EMAIL — formatted emails to custom recipients. SEND NOTIFICATION — notification over multiple Channels. PUSH NOTIFICATION — iOS/Android mobile alert for a pending Case action. POST TO PULSE — posts a message to the Pulse feed.
Key Automation shapes available in the Process modeler:
items: Run Data Transform: executes a Data Transform at runtime
Connect Generative AI: calls a GenAI model and maps the response
Decision: branches the flow via a When rule or Decision Table
Wait: pauses the Case until a condition or timer fires

elements.caption: App Studio offers 18 Automation shapes. Memorize them by group: Stage navigation, Case actions, Documents & content, Communication, Logic & AI, Flow control. Note the pairs that are easy to confuse — Create PDF (from a View) vs Generate document, and Push notification (mobile) vs Send notification (multi-Channel).

elements.description: Send automated email correspondence to all relevant parties with no user interaction. Example: an online store emails a customer about new offers. You configure how the application determines the recipient and compose the email content.

Run a selected Data Transform rule at runtime to set/copy/initialize Case data. Example: at checkout, if the billing address equals the shipping address, a Data Transform copies it automatically instead of making the customer re-enter it.

elements.title: Automation Shape Selector

examPitfalls.title: Automation = system, no Assignment
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask whether an Automation step creates an Assignment for a user. Candidates say yes, expecting all steps to require human action. Automation steps are executed by the system — they do not create Assignments and do not appear in any user's Worklist.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: If a Step needs no user input, use an Automation shape — not a Collect information Step.

examPitfalls.title: Create PDF vs Generate document
examPitfalls.trapDescription: These are two SEPARATE shapes. Create PDF renders a specified View into a PDF and attaches it; Generate document generates Case documents as part of the Case Life Cycle.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: PDF from a specific View → Create PDF. Case documents in the lifecycle → Generate document. (Constellation apps need a workaround for Create PDF.)

examPitfalls.title: Push notification vs Send notification vs Send email
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Push notification = iOS/Android mobile device. Send notification = recipients over MULTIPLE Channels. Send email = formatted emails to custom recipients. They are not interchangeable.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Read the channel carefully: mobile device → Push notification; multi-Channel alert → Send notification; email message → Send email.

examPitfalls.title: Three Stage shapes, not one
examPitfalls.trapDescription: There are separate shapes for Change to a Stage (specific), Change to next Stage, and Change to the previous Stage.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Pick the exact Stage shape: specific target, next, or previously visited.

examPitfalls.title: Persist Case = temporary → permanent
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Persist Case converts a temporary Case into a permanent object in the database — it is not a generic 'save data' step.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use Persist Case when a temporary Case must become permanent (e.g., before resolution or for integrations).

examPitfalls.title: Wait pauses on a condition
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Wait pauses the Case until a specified condition is met — a timer OR a Case status (e.g., child Cases resolved).
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Need to hold the Case until something happens → Wait shape.

examPitfalls.title: Where to add Automations
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The add path differs by tool: Case Life Cycle uses Step > More > Automations; the Process modeler uses Add > Automations.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Remember both entry points; the exam may name either tool.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Step must generate a PDF from a specified View and attach it to the Case automatically, with no user interaction. Which Automation shape does this?

options.text: Create PDF — creates a PDF file from a specified View and attaches it to the Case
Collect information — displays a form to the user who must enter the PDF content manually
Attach content — the user attaches the View as a file to the Case
Questionnaire — the user completes a questionnaire that outputs the PDF

practiceQuiz.hint: PDF from a specified View, attached automatically = Create PDF.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Create PDF creates a PDF file from a specified View and attaches it to the Case with no user interaction B is wrong because Collect information is a user-facing form..

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Case should automatically spin off one or more related Cases when it reaches a specific Step. Which Automation shape?

options.text: Create Case — creates one or more Cases from the current Case automatically
Change to a Stage — moves the current Case to a different Stage, which spawns a Case
Update a Case — updating the current Case automatically creates its child Cases
Wait — pauses the Case until a child Case is created manually

practiceQuiz.hint: Create one or more Cases from the current Case = Create Case.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Create Case creates one or more Cases from the current Case B is wrong because Change to a Stage moves the current Case to a Stage — it does.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Generate document and Create PDF are both document-related Automation shapes. What is the key distinction tested on the exam?

options.text: Create PDF renders a specified View into a PDF and attaches it; Generate document generates Case documents as part of the Case Life Cycle
They are the same shape with two names; either generates any document from any source
Create PDF works only in Constellation; Generate document works only in the legacy UI
Generate document attaches files to a Case; Create PDF sends them by email

practiceQuiz.hint: One renders a View to PDF; the other generates Case documents.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Create PDF creates a PDF from a specified View and attaches it; Generate document generates Case documents as part of the lifecycle. They are distinct shapes (B wrong).

practiceQuiz.scenario: At the end of a Process the system must run a Data Transform rule to copy the shipping address into the billing address fields — no Assignment, no message. Which shape?

options.text: Run Data Transform — runs the selected Data Transform rule at runtime to set/copy Case data without user interaction
Approve/Reject — automatically evaluates the addresses and approves the copy
Send notification — notifies the customer that the addresses were copied
Connect Generative AI — prompts Pega GenAI to copy the address values

practiceQuiz.hint: Run a Data Transform at runtime to copy fields = Run Data Transform.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Run Data Transform executes a Data Transform rule at runtime to copy/initialize Case data — the exact checkout use case. B is wrong because Approve/Reject is a human decision step. C is wrong because Send notification sends a message, not field copies. D is wrong because Connect Generative AI is for GenAI prompts/responses, not deterministic field copying.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which THREE of the following are Automation shapes available in App Studio?

options.text: Search duplicate Cases — automatically searches for duplicate Cases using set conditions
Post to Pulse — creates a message and posts it to the Pulse social stream
Connect Generative AI — uses customized Pega GenAI rules (define prompt and response structure)
Call REST API — invokes an external REST service directly as an Automation shape

practiceQuiz.hint: Three are in the App Studio Automation table; one is not.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Search duplicate Cases, Post to Pulse, and Connect Generative AI are all Automation shapes in App Studio. D is wrong because 'Call REST API' is not one of the App Studio Automation shapes — integrations are handled differently (e.g., through connectors/Data Pages), not via a 'Call REST API' Automation shape.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A parent Case must pause until all its child Cases are resolved before continuing. Which Automation shape?

options.text: Wait — pauses the Case until a specified condition is fulfilled, such as a timer or a Case status
Persist Case — pauses the Case until the children are written to the database
Change to next Stage — advances the Case, which waits for children automatically
Update a Case — updating children pauses the parent until they finish

practiceQuiz.hint: Pause until a condition (timer / Case status) = Wait.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Wait pauses the Case until a condition is met — a timer or a Case status such as child Cases reaching resolution B is wrong because Persist Case converts a temporary Case to permanent — it does not pause..

practiceQuiz.scenario: An unsaved (temporary) Case must become a permanent record in the database at a specific point so an integration can read it. Which shape?

options.text: Persist Case — converts a temporary Case to a permanent object in the database
Update a Case — updates the current Case, which also commits it to the database
Attach content — attaching a file forces the Case to be saved
Generate document — generating a document persists the Case as a side effect

practiceQuiz.hint: Temporary → permanent in the DB = Persist Case.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Persist Case converts a temporary Case into a permanent object in the database. B is wrong because Update a Case updates Case data (current Case or children/descendants) and is not the shape defined for converting temporary to permanent. C and D are wrong because attaching content or generating a document are not mechanisms for persisting a temporary Case.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A workflow must alert participants over multiple Channels (not just email, not just mobile) when a milestone is reached. Which shape?

options.text: Send notification — sends a notification to recipients over multiple Channels
Push notification — sends a notification to an iOS or Android mobile device
Send email — sends formatted emails to custom recipients
Post to Pulse — posts a message to the Pulse social stream

practiceQuiz.hint: Which automation shape delivers notifications to recipients across multiple channels simultaneously?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Send notification delivers a notification to recipients over multiple Channels. B is wrong because Push notification targets a mobile device specifically. C is wrong because Send email is email only. D is wrong because Post to Pulse writes to the social stream, a single mechanism, not multi-Channel notification.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega developer is reviewing the Automation shapes available in App Studio for a Claims workflow and wants to confirm how these shapes behave when the Case reaches them at runtime. Which statement correctly describes how Automation shapes execute during Case processing?

options.text: They run automatically when the Case reaches the Step — no Assignment is created and no user action is required
They always display a form and wait for user input before executing
They can only be added in the Process modeler, never in the Case Life Cycle
They authenticate the operator before each Automation executes

practiceQuiz.hint: Automation shapes auto-execute at runtime: no Assignment, no user action required.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Automation shapes (yellow rectangles) execute system logic automatically without creating an Assignment and without requiring any user input. They contrast with Collect Information or Questionnaire shapes, which pause flow to present a form to the user. Common automations include Send Email, Create Case, and Run Data Transform — all triggered by the system, not the user.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A requirement says: update not only the current Case but all of its child Cases and descendants in one Automation. Which shape?

options.text: Update a Case — updates the current Case or all child Cases and descendants
Create Case — creates the children and updates them at the same time
Run Data Transform — a Data Transform always cascades to child Cases automatically
Change to a Stage — moving Stage updates all descendants

practiceQuiz.hint: Update current Case OR all children/descendants = Update a Case.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Update a Case can update the current Case or all child Cases and descendants B is wrong because Create Case creates new Cases, it does not bulk-update existing descendants..

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA needs an Automation that uses customized Pega GenAI rules — defining the prompt sent to the model and the structure of the response. Which shape, and what is the prerequisite?

options.text: Connect Generative AI — and generative AI must be enabled/configured in the application settings
Run Data Transform — no prerequisite; Data Transforms include GenAI prompts
Send notification — GenAI responses are delivered as notifications
Questionnaire — GenAI fills the questionnaire answers automatically

practiceQuiz.hint: GenAI prompt + response structure = Connect Generative AI (needs GenAI enabled).
practiceQuiz.rationale: Connect Generative AI uses customized Pega GenAI rules; you define the prompt and the response structure, and generative AI must be enabled/configured in application settings. B, C, and D describe unrelated shapes that do not provide GenAI prompt/response configuration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO statements correctly pair a need with the right Stage-navigation Automation shape?

options.text: Return the Case to the Stage it was in before → Change to the previous Stage
Advance the Case to the following Stage automatically → Change to next Stage
Jump to any specific Stage → Change to next Stage
Advance to the following Stage → Change to a Stage

practiceQuiz.hint: Previous = previously visited; next = the following Stage; specific target = Change to a Stage.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Change to the previous Stage returns to the previously visited Stage (A correct); Change to next Stage advances to the following Stage (B correct) C is wrong because jumping to a specific Stage requires Change to a Stage, not Change to next.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is selecting Automation shapes to add system-executed steps to a Claims workflow. Which TWO statements correctly describe how Automation shapes behave in Pega Case processing?

options.text: Automation shapes execute system actions — such as sending emails, creating child Cases, or calling services — without requiring user interaction
Automation shapes can be placed in a Case Life Cycle to run automatically when the Case reaches that step in the workflow
Automation shapes always require a human approver to confirm the action before the automation executes
Automation shapes in App Studio are restricted to sending emails and cannot perform other types of system actions

practiceQuiz.hint: Automations run without user interaction and execute automatically at their step — no human approval needed.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Decision shape adds conditional branching or skipping. It evaluates conditions automatically — no user action. Automation shapes like Send Email execute system tasks. Flow Actions define user interactions.

quickRecap.value: System action that runs automatically — no Assignment, no user input. Saves time, configurable, reduces error.
Case Life Cycle: Step > More > Automations. Process modeler: Add > Automations.
Change to a Stage (specific) · Change to next Stage · Change to the previous Stage.
Create Case (one+ from current) · Update a Case (self/children/descendants) · Persist Case (temp→permanent) · Search duplicate Cases.
Attach content (file/URL/note) · Create PDF (from a View) · Generate document (Case documents).
Send email (custom recipients) · Send notification (multi-Channel) · Push notification (mobile device) · Post to Pulse.
Run Data Transform · Connect Generative AI (needs GenAI enabled) · Wait (timer/Case status) · Questionnaire (user completes).
